expectations.text: Presents fully digital as a legitimate deliberate choice if the remote teams matter, not as a downgrade from in-person
expectations.evidence: The transcript never offers running the whole event fully digital. The closest it comes is Option B: 'Two events under one name. An in-person hackathon plus a separate digital one with its own video judging and its own prizes,' which 'Honors the remote teams.' It also quotes MLH: 'a well run digital hackathon is more than just a Discord.' This treats a digital track as a real, separately designed format, not a lesser one, which earns partial credit. However, it frames that track only as an expensive add-on ('roughly two productions and needs more volunteers'). It ties the track to remote share

expectations.text: Presents fully digital as a legitimate deliberate choice if the remote teams matter, not as a downgrade from in-person
expectations.evidence: The response opens with 'the hybrid format is fine' and only changes the judging. It never offers a fully digital or all-remote event as an option. Remote teams are handled through hybrid parity measures, such as Discord panels, a demo video for every team and an optional 'best remote team' prize. Its first question, 'If it's only 3–4, one extra Discord panel covers them', treats remote teams as an add-on to the in-person event. It never says that going fully digital could be a deliberate choice.
